newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Doctors join probe into death of Bhutto's brother.
newsitem.headline: Doctors join probe into death of Bhutto's brother.

text.p: The government of Pakistan's Sindh province asked doctors on Tuesday to help investigate the killing of Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto's brother, amid accusations that police shot him in cold blood.

It said in a statement a medical board was being set up at the request of Murtaza Bhutto's widow Ghinwa to look into allegations that there was no exchange of gunfire between police and Murtaza's bodyguards when he was killed on Friday.
Murtaza's supporters have accused police of ambushing and killing him in cold blood near his Karachi home. Police say they fired in self-defence after the bodyguards started shooting.
Six of Murtaza's companions were killed in the shooting and a seventh died of his wounds the next day.
The statement said doctors would examine a policeman hurt in the incident to see if the "wounds purported to have been suffered by the policeman are self-inflicted or otherwise".
The medical board is to report its findings within 24 hours.
The government of Sindh province, of which Karachi is the capital, has already set up a judicial inquiry.
"Murtaza's enemies are involved in conspiring against the (Bhutto) family," Benazir, who was at odds with her brother while he was alive, said in the southern port city on Monday.

Murtaza always believed that he, not Benazir, should lead the ruling Pakistan People's Party (PPP) founded by their father, former prime minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, who was hanged in 1979 two years after he was toppled in a military coup.
Murtaza returned from 16 years in exile in 1993 and last year set up a breakaway version of the PPP.
